bearings.paper_claim: Participation persistence: P(lobby this year given lobbied last year) = 92 percent in a balanced 3,260-firm Compustat panel, 1998-2006 (6.2 percent lobby in a given year; 10.0 percent ever lobby). Above 80 percent in almost all two-digit NAICS industries. 96 percent of expenditures in a typical year come from prior-year lobbyists. Entry clusters in the year before an election, not the election year; exit is unrelated to the cycle.
bearings.paper_location: Sec 2 p.7 (92 percent, 80 percent, 96 percent, entry and exit timing); Table 1 (6.2 and 10.0 percent)
bearings.system_side: Mentat lobbying projection is the one quantity exempt from the midterm/presidential phase adjustment (Phase 6 owner rulings of 2026-10-01, README paragraph near line 152). Calculator rule: last year plus slope times predicted-growth change, with no year effect (rf_v2model.R line 132).
bearings.transfer_conditions: Evidence is participation for 1998-2006 public firms, not sector dollars. The 96 percent is one sample's expenditure share. Election timing in the paper concerns entry, a small share of dollars, so it does not show phase has zero effect on spend; that stays untested here.
bearings.verifier_note: All paper figures confirmed in text and Table 1; code exemption confirmed in README and calculator line. Analyst transfer caveat is correct and should stay. This supports the design; it does not validate forecast accuracy.

bearings.paper_claim: Lagged lobbying status raises current-year lobbying probability by 0.84 to 0.88 in Blundell-Bond columns 2-6 (baseline column 2 = 0.8848; column 6 = 0.8810), 26,080 firm-years, 1998-2006 public firms (Table 2 and note). Table 7 Panel E: 0.00 entry 2004-2006 among the most dependent firms not lobbying in 2001-2003, on both LCA and patenting measures. Entry is not zero elsewhere: 4th-quintile LCA non-lobbyists show 0.08, and Nike entered without prior lobbying (fn 26).
bearings.paper_location: pp.10-12, Table 2 and note; pp.17-19, Table 7 Panel E, fn 26
bearings.system_side: Mentat G9: log-lobbying refit MAE 4.050 vs naive 3.936 (README line 142; test-08-backtest.R line 61 pins 3.936); confirmed. Sector-study backtest triple (MAE 3.63 vs 3.99 with growth and 6.55 with control terms, LobbyView 2014-2023) was NOT found in any file under the sector_growth_study folder; unverified. Bands as split-conformal persistence errors, targets 2014-2023, horizons 1-3: confirmed in rf_lobbying.R persistence function.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Persistence evidence is for binary participation, not dollars. The naive-anchor result for dollars holds only while incumbents dominate sector totals; entrant-heavy sectors (crypto before 2015, fintech) break that. The no-entry result holds only for the top dependency quintile, not all dependent firms.
bearings.verifier_note: Table values confirmed (columns 2-6 range 0.8448 to 0.8848; columns 7-8 0.4429 and 0.3385). Softened because the no-entry claim omits the 4th-quintile LCA 8 percent and the Nike exception, and the sector backtest MAE triple is not located. Drop the unlocated triple until a file reproduces it.

bearings.paper_claim: Short panel (T=9, 1998-2006). Within-firm FE OLS gives 0.44 (column 7; column 8 gives 0.34), which the authors expect to be biased downward following Nickell 1981. Blundell-Bond GMM with lag-two instruments gives 0.84-0.88 (columns 2-6). Arellano-Bond is more sensitive across variants; its point estimate is 0.52 (SE 0.18) in Appendix Table 3 column 2, which the analyst omitted.
bearings.paper_location: pp.10-12; Table 2 columns 2-8; Appendix Table 3 column 2
bearings.system_side: Brain sector-growth topic (line 269) transcribes the original contract equation (3) as log Lobby = alpha_i + rho times lagged log Lobby + growth terms + phase terms, with 5 sector clusters noted. The claim that implemented core L tests are levels with sector FE and no lagged outcome, and that only SEATS-W carries a lagged-outcome sensitivity, was not verified line by line in sgs_registry.R.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The Nickell-bias order (1+rho)/(T-1) is a textbook approximation, not a Kerr result; applying it to Mentat is new agent analysis and stays UNVERIFIED (DE-062). The claim that GMM is not feasible with 5 clusters has no source in Kerr or the brain and was not verified.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper numbers confirmed (column 7 0.4429, column 8 0.3385, BB 0.84-0.88, pp.10-12). Softened: add the Arellano-Bond 0.52 point estimate and drop the GMM-with-5-clusters claim. The Nickell reading remains UNVERIFIED.

bearings.paper_claim: Mean annual sales 5,407 ($m) for lobbying firms vs 1,423 for non-lobbying firms (Table 1; 327 lobbying firms of 3,260, 1998-2006). Policy response identified from 2001 dependence times a 2004-2006 binding-cap dummy with firm and year FE; high-skilled lobbying 0.043 (SE 0.014) per log LCA count (Table 5, 846 core obs). Falsification on unrelated issues is null (pp.15-16).
bearings.paper_location: Table 1; eq (3) on p.16; Table 5 p.17; pp.15-16
bearings.system_side: Growth adds no adjusted R2: 0.884717 with predicted growth vs 0.884690 without, on 77 rows (Codex review note in sgs_review.R line 237, also in brain). L3-LV growth coefficient flips from +0.352 to -0.477 with sector and year FE (brain). Both confirmed.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Kerr shows size predicts who lobbies, and that the 2004 response came from already-lobbying firms changing issues. Kerr does not show that yearly changes follow shared issue shocks, which the analyst text claims. A dated CU or bank policy design would be a new preregistered estimand, not a rescue of the growth tests.
bearings.verifier_note: Page for eq (3) corrected from p.14 to p.16. Numbers confirmed. Softened: the changes-follow-shocks sentence is analyst inference, not Kerr; Kerr says size matters more at the extensive margin than the intensive one.

bearings.paper_claim: LDA filings do not require an amount per specific topic (p.19). Issue intensity is proxied by the number of years a topic is listed and by keyword matches in specific-issue text (H-1B, L-1, PERM, high-skill bills), pp.5-6.
bearings.system_side: contested_bills.py allowed record keys are bill, congress, mode, counterparty_industries, active_from, active_to, ratified_by, ratified_date and note; there is no spend field. Engine wiring and the bank-vs-CU spend question were not checked.
bearings.transfer_conditions: A relative-spend test per bill needs report dollars apportioned across issues and bills, which Kerr avoids; a filing or issue-mention count is the defensible proxy. LDA stays an identity and measurement source, never an edge or weight (D-021).
bearings.verifier_note: Paper claim confirmed on p.19 and pp.5-6; system fields confirmed. Analyst wording that LDA reports cannot measure per-issue spend is slightly stronger than the paper, which says only that amounts per topic are not required; keep the narrower wording.

related.why: Item title matches the Bombardini and Trebbi 2020 survey of empirical lobbying models. Kerr does not cite it; its coverage of fixed-cost and participation models is unverified from the item file.
Corrected from same-data. Kerr uses CRP and SOPR LDA filings (pp.5-6), not the LobbyView database. LobbyView is the source of Mentat's sector-year series, so the link is by data family only.
Corrected from builds-on. Kerr does not cite Huneeus and Kim. Shared fixed-cost and selection theme is an analyst judgment, not a documented lineage.
Item title covers lobbying ROI under the 2004 American Jobs Creation Act, a 2004 policy event; Kerr does not cite it. Returns view versus Kerr's participation view is consistent with the title.
Item title covers the timing of donations relative to lobbying, which bears on Kerr's pre-election entry result. Kerr does not cite it.
Item title covers change over time in the US lobbying network, a network-level counterpart to Kerr's firm-level persistence facts.
Item title is a review of empirical lobbying research (NBER WP 19698). Kerr does not cite it; the framing claim is unverified from the item file.
Item title links corporate lobbying and PACs to firm size and market concentration, extending Kerr's size gradient. Kerr does not cite it.

summary_issues: Summary asserts the AEJ Economic Policy version is dated 2014. The analyst text is the NBER WP 17577 of November 2011 and the AEJ version is not in the file; unverified here.
Summary says dependence does not raise the chance of lobbying at all (-0.008, SE 0.009). That is a negative insignificant LCA any-issue estimate (Table 5 column 3); say no detectable effect.

Summary says no highly dependent non-lobbyist entered. True only for the most dependent quintile (0.00 on both measures, Table 7 Panel E). The 4th-quintile LCA non-lobbyists show 0.08 entry, and Nike entered in 2004 without prior lobbying (fn 26).
Summary says the paper backs Mentat persistence-anchored lobbying forecasts. Evidence is on firm participation, not sector dollars; say it is consistent with the design, with the transfer caveat.
Summary says LDA reports cannot measure spending per issue. The paper says only that amounts per specific topic are not required (p.19); reports do list totals.

ext key_findings 10 and the paper p.18 say the Table 6 interaction t-statistics are under 0.5. Table 6 LCA interaction is -0.013 (SE 0.020), t about -0.65; patenting 0.008 (SE 0.022), t about 0.36. The error is inherited from the paper text.

flags: the claim that Kerr dollar figures do not distinguish in-house from outside-firm spend cites fn 6, but fn 6 says the model abstracts from the in-house versus outside choice. Paper p.5 says filings report in-house and external totals separately; the flag is unsupported as written.

paul_alignment (not summary): Paul's cycle-model note says lobbying peaks in election years, and Paul holds that returns motivate deep pockets. Item has no Paul annotations (paul_entries empty); neither statement was found in the refit README or the brain topic files checked.
Sector-study backtest MAE values (3.63, 3.99, 6.55) cited in bearing 2 were not located in the sector_growth_study files; treat as unverified until a file reproduces them.
